title: Autonomous Software Factory — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. PROPOSED CAPABILITY TARGET. This record describes a proposed future-grade capability target from the source paste. It is a specification of what such a tool would do, NOT a claim that it has been implemented, tested, or proven. A tool specification alone does not make an otherwise impossible technology achievable. Some entries build on existing research; others would require major scientific breakthroughs, new hardware, or extensive engineering. Generates, builds, tests, packages, and maintains families of related applications. A proposed factory that treats applications as manufactured products: from a product line definition it generates variants, builds them, runs test suites, packages releases, and maintains them over time — applying patches, updating dependencies, and retiring obsolete variants. The factory keeps a bill of materials for every build so any release can be reproduced. The paste flags this as one of the five most powerful tools to build first, because it can help create the other tools.
capabilities: Generate application variants from a product-line definition
Build and run full test suites automatically
Package releases with reproducible bills of materials
Maintain apps: patch, update dependencies, retire variants
Track failures across the family to fix root causes once
